To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a full 3d voxel-based map can be created from stereo vision, that the map can be used to detect moving obstacles, and that the speed of moving obstacles can be estimated from egomotion.

we present a flexible approach to build, in realtime, a dense voxelized map of the environment using a 3D laser scanner or a 3D camera; the voxelized map is then processed using a flood-fill approach to discriminate between static and dynamic obstacles; the egomotion computed by a stereo-based visual odometry system allows the estimation of the absolute speed of the dynamic obstacles.

(1) we propose a flexible technique to detect and track obstacles in urban scenarios, using a stereo system and a voxel-based representation; (2) we use the egomotion to improve the computational efficiency of the voxel-based representation; we also use the egomotions to provide an estimation of the absolute speed of detected obstacles; (3) we tested the algorithm on one of Vislab's AGVs using the modified SGM-based system as 3-D data source.
